architecture.summary: The fleet command delete now reads the organization in WorkOS before its confirmation and takes the cause of the removal from that read, as the weekly organization sweep does (owner decision of 2 November 2026): an organization that WorkOS no longer has gives organization-absent, so the deleted row loses organization_name, and the documented account-deletion path (remove the WorkOS organization, then fleet.ts delete) leaves no organization name in the registry; an organization that WorkOS has gives operator, so the row keeps the name and the repair "delete, then request" gives the revived row the same service name. A read that fails stops the command before the confirmation, with nothing changed; a row that is deleted already gets no read. The decision is removalCauseOf of the tenants removal, a pure function with two unit cases; the delete command of the fleet script gains the WorkOS organization inventory read that the request and summary commands already make, and needs the existing WorkOS settings (internalInterface: the removal contract of tenants and the collaboration of the fleet script with the workos adapter change). The data retention of the account deletion procedure changes again (sensitiveBehavior). The row write of an absent organization needs the column organization_name of #319, so the command now has that migration as a prerequisite too; without the column it deletes the Render service and fails the row write. No new column, migration, setting, or grant; no component, container, public module, dependency, or Mermaid view changes; the prose of the tenant registry view records the cause of the command.
